Here's an example from my STAR answers I've typed out:

1. **Give me an example of a time when you had to deal with a difficult co-worker or fellow student on a project. How did you handle the situation? What were the outcomes?**
    
    Senior Capstone Project → Worked as part of a group, and was project manager in charge of assigning tasks → As part of the project, gathered some data from student participants → Wanted to perform data analysis to show our findings and put it on our expo poster to present at the end of the semester → I put teammate in charge of data analysis, who reports back with AI generated plots and tables → AI was a valuable tool throughout our work, but I was concerned → Didn’t know how the AI generated the results, let alone if those methods were valid → Brought up my concerns with the teammate → Found that he was just enthused about the efficiency of AI, but he understood my concerns → We redid the analysis with more manual techniques, though still using AI assistance, to be sure of the validity of our methods → Our capstone advisor was impressed with our poster and our display of our results → The expo was a success, with many students and judges engaging with our project

What I recommend: 
- First: write/type your answers out yourself. Doing this will reinforce most of your answer in your brain since you're using the brain power to generate it in the first place and paying attention to writing/typing it down.
- Second: when you write your answers, don't write like you're writing an essay. What I mean is, don't write like what you're writing is meant to be read by someone else. When you're telling a story, it's cause and effect (I was in X situation, and we had X problem, so my approach was to do Y...blah blah). So when you write your answer, write the train of thought. This way you're writing a series of phrases, which will be a lot easier to memorize than a paragraph. Basically, I'm telling you not to write complete sentences and write the way you think. I'll show you an example, because I may just have written the most confusing explanation of all time.
